change: Ch. 11 §1 p. 949 identifies prenuclear interrogative phrase plus uninverted subject–predicator order as one marker of subordinate interrogative form; the corresponding main interrogative typically has inversion.

Ch. 11 §1 p. 950 confirms that finite subordinate clauses include subjunctives despite use of the plain form, as well as clauses with present, preterite or irrealis forms. Non-finite clauses include infinitival, gerund-participial and past-participial constructions.

Ch. 11 §1 p. 950 confirms relative, comparative and content as the principal finite subordinate types; content is the default, lacking the special gap properties of relative and comparative clauses. This does not convert the descriptive default into a grammatical prohibition.
Ch. 11 §1 p. 950 explicitly describes supplementary wh-relatives as subordinate in form, though supplements are not integrated syntactic dependents.
